frontier.hypothesis: Target's source carries an EIGHTH arg1 reference that post-reload jump2 cross-jumping deletes, at a site other than the `<` arm (which is spoken for by the store pin) and other than the `>` path (killed as P5). Finding that site closes cluster A, the store sink and the arm store simultaneously and lands near 4-6 / 215.
frontier.mechanism: reg_n_refs is computed by regclass before local_alloc; jump_optimize with cross-jumping runs AFTER reload, so a duplicated call pair is visible to allocno_compare but absent from the final asm. The s16 body demonstrates the mechanism end-to-end: its duplicated `<`-arm call pair raises nrefs(arg1) to 9, wins cluster A, and is merged away post-RA leaving 216 insns. The requirement is a duplicate whose two copies CONVERGE on a common successor (so find_cross_jump has a mergeable tail) - P5 failed precisely because its two arms diverge immediately after the calls.

frontier.hypothesis: Body P4's 16-point residual is entirely prologue register displacement caused by the live incoming $a1, and part of it may be recoverable without touching the carrier - which would make solution (b) competitive with solution (a) after all.
frontier.mechanism: The carrier's source operand is $a1, live from entry to block_15, so the range-check chain is pushed off $a1 and $a2 onto $a3 and $t0. If the chain's two scratch values can be made to prefer registers that are free anyway - e.g. by respelling `temp_a1 = *(u16 *)(arg0 + 0x6A)` and the 4/0x14 comparison constants so their pseudos get different preferred classes - the rename cascade may collapse even with $a1 pinned, leaving only the `move s2,a1` position (~2 pts).
frontier.next_probe: On P4 (rejected/s21-late-arg1-carrier-flips-seats-but-pins-a1-16.c), diff emitted 3-50 against target insn by insn and count how many of the 10 points are the a1->a3 / a2->t0 renames versus the `move s2,a1` position. Then try moving `p = arg1;` to the earliest point that still keeps livelen(p) <= 65 (the threshold is 2*7*10000/L > 2142, i.e. L <= 65; P4 measures 58, so there is slack) and re-read ALLOCDBG - an earlier assignment shortens $a1's pinned span and may free the chain's registers back.
